ar: عَنْ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَبِي حَفْصٍ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ: «إنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى، فَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَهِجْرَتُهُ إلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، وَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ لِدُنْيَا يُصِيبُهَا أَوْ امْرَأَةٍ يَنْكِحُهَا فَهِجْرَتُهُ إلَى مَا هَاجَرَ إلَيْهِ».

s: This is the hadith with which Imam al-Bukhari opens his Sahih, and with which an-Nawawi opens his Forty. The narrator is ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, who is said to have stated it from the pulpit of the Prophet’s mosque in Madinah. It has a remarkable chain: it came down through a single narrator at each of its first three levels and became widely transmitted only after that, which scholars call a gharib hadith that was then received by the whole community.

Some commentators mention a background: a man who migrated from Makkah to Madinah not for the sake of Allah but to marry a woman called Umm Qays, and so was known as “the emigrant of Umm Qays”. This report is cited by a number of the scholars, though its chain is discussed. The hadith itself does not depend on it.
m: “Actions are by intentions” (innama l-a‘malu bin-niyyat). The word niyyah means purpose: the direction of the heart toward a goal. Scholars explain that intention does three things. It separates worship from habit: the same act of washing or eating may be a custom or an act of worship, according to what the heart intends. It separates one act of worship from another: the two rak‘ahs of Fajr from the sunnah before it. And it decides the value of an act: whom it is for.

The hadith then gives its own example, emigration. Whoever’s emigration was for Allah and His Messenger, it is for Allah and His Messenger; whoever’s was for something of this world to gain, or a woman to marry, his emigration is for what he emigrated to. Same journey, same road, same hardship, but one is worship and the other is travel.

Imam ash-Shafi‘i and Imam Ahmad are reported to have said that this hadith holds a third of all knowledge, since the work of a person is of the heart, the tongue and the limbs, and the intention is the work of the heart, which is the greatest of the three.
l: Before you begin any act of worship, and any permitted act too, renew the intention: this is for Allah.
Turn ordinary things into worship by intending them for His sake: work to provide, eating to strengthen, sleep to rest for prayer.
Check your sincerity often; it is easier to lose than to find.

en: On the authority of the Commander of the Believers, Abu Hafs ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Actions are only by intentions, and every person will have only what he intended. So whoever’s emigration was to Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever’s emigration was for some worldly gain that he would get, or a woman whom he would marry, his emigration is to that for which he emigrated.”

ar: عَنْ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَيْضًا قَالَ: بَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ جُلُوسٌ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ، إذْ طَلَعَ عَلَيْنَا رَجُلٌ شَدِيدُ بَيَاضِ الثِّيَابِ، شَدِيدُ سَوَادِ الشَّعْرِ، لَا يُرَى عَلَيْهِ أَثَرُ السَّفَرِ، وَلَا يَعْرِفُهُ مِنَّا أَحَدٌ. حَتَّى جَلَسَ إلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم. فَأَسْنَدَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إلَى رُكْبَتَيْهِ، وَوَضَعَ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ، وَقَالَ: يَا مُحَمَّدُ أَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ الْإِسْلَامِ. فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم الْإِسْلَامُ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَنْ لَا إلَهَ إلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَتُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِيَ الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ، وَتَحُجَّ الْبَيْتَ إنْ اسْتَطَعْت إلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا. قَالَ: صَدَقْت. فَعَجِبْنَا لَهُ يَسْأَلُهُ وَيُصَدِّقُهُ! قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ الْإِيمَانِ. قَالَ: أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاَللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ. قَالَ: صَدَقْت. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ الْإِحْسَانِ. قَالَ: أَنْ تَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ كَأَنَّك تَرَاهُ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ تَرَاهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَرَاك. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ السَّاعَةِ. قَالَ: مَا الْمَسْئُولُ عَنْهَا بِأَعْلَمَ مِنْ السَّائِلِ. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ أَمَارَاتِهَا؟ قَالَ: أَنْ تَلِدَ الْأَمَةُ رَبَّتَهَا، وَأَنْ تَرَى الْحُفَاةَ الْعُرَاةَ الْعَالَةَ رِعَاءَ الشَّاءِ يَتَطَاوَلُونَ فِي الْبُنْيَانِ. ثُمَّ انْطَلَقَ، فَلَبِثْتُ مَلِيًّا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: يَا عُمَرُ أَتَدْرِي مَنْ السَّائِلُ؟. قُلْتُ: اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ. قَالَ: فَإِنَّهُ جِبْرِيلُ أَتَاكُمْ يُعَلِّمُكُمْ دِينَكُمْ.

s: Muslim reports this from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, and it is known as the hadith of Jibril. It reads like a scene from a play, and ‘Umar tells it in the first person. They were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day when a man appeared in front of them whose clothes were extremely white and whose hair was extremely black. There was no sign of travel on him, and none of them knew him. He came and sat down with his knees touching the Prophet’s knees and placed his palms on his thighs.

Then he asked his questions, one after the other: What is Islam? What is faith (iman)? What is excellence (ihsan)? When is the Hour? And what are its signs? The Prophet ﷺ answered each, and the stranger said “You have spoken truly” after each, which astonished the listeners: he asks and then confirms. Then he left. After a while the Prophet ﷺ said, “O ‘Umar, do you know who the questioner was?” ‘Umar said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said, “That was Jibril. He came to teach you your religion.”
m: The hadith gives the religion in three levels. Islam is the outward: the testimony, prayer, zakat, fasting and Hajj. Iman is the inward: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the divine decree, its good and its bad. Ihsan is the depth: to worship Allah as though you see Him, for if you do not see Him, He sees you. Scholars note that the three are a progression from the body, to the mind and heart, to the presence of the soul.

On the Hour, the Prophet ﷺ said that the one asked knows no more than the one asking, and then gave two signs: that a slave woman will give birth to her mistress (understood by commentators as a reversal of social orders or of children’s attitudes to parents), and that you will see the barefoot, ill-clad, destitute shepherds competing in building tall structures. These signs describe social upheaval and display.
l: Examine your practice at the three levels: do you pray, do you believe, do you worship with presence?
Make the sentence of ihsan your standard in prayer: Allah sees you.
Do not be preoccupied with when the Hour is. Be ready for it.

en:
On the authority of ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), who also said: One day, while we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man appeared before us whose clothes were extremely white and whose hair was extremely black. No sign of travel could be seen on him, and none of us knew him. He sat down in front of the Prophet ﷺ, rested his knees against his knees, placed his palms on his thighs, and said: “O Muhammad, tell me about Islam.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Islam is to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish the prayer, to give zakat, to fast Ramadan, and to make the pilgrimage to the House if you are able to find a way to it.” He said: “You have spoken truly.” We were amazed at him: he asks him, and then confirms that he is right!

He said: “Tell me about iman (faith).” He said: “It is to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day, and to believe in the divine decree, its good and its bad.” He said: “You have spoken truly.” He said: “Tell me about ihsan (excellence).” He said: “It is to worship Allah as though you see Him; and if you do not see Him, then truly He sees you.” He said: “Tell me about the Hour.” He said: “The one being asked knows no more about it than the one asking.” He said: “Then tell me about its signs.” He said: “That the slave woman will give birth to her mistress, and that you will see barefoot, unclothed, destitute shepherds competing in building tall buildings.”

Then he went away, and I stayed for a while. Then the Prophet ﷺ said to me: “O ‘Umar, do you know who the questioner was?” I said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “It was Jibril. He came to teach you your religion.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: سَمِعْت رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَقُولُ: بُنِيَ الْإِسْلَامُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ: شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لَا إلَهَ إلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَإِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ، وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ، وَحَجِّ الْبَيْتِ، وَصَوْمِ رَمَضَانَ.

s: Al-Bukhari and Muslim report this from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar. A narration in al-Bukhari gives a scene from the civil strife among Muslims in Ibn ‘Umar’s later years. A man asked why he would not join the fighting. Ibn ‘Umar answered that Allah had forbidden the shedding of a Muslim’s blood, and then recalled what matters most: that Islam is built on five.
m: The image of a building: a structure on five pillars. The testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger is the foundation. Prayer, zakat, fasting Ramadan and Hajj stand upon it. Remove one and the building is damaged; the tent pole of the structure is the testimony.

A detail from Muslim’s narration: a man said “Hajj and fasting Ramadan”, putting Hajj before fasting. Ibn ‘Umar corrected him: “No, fasting Ramadan and Hajj: this is how I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He was careful about the order and the wording.
l: Take stock of each pillar: where is the building leaning?
Make sure the foundation, your faith in Allah and His Messenger, is deepened by knowledge.
Teach children the five early and with love.

en: On the authority of Abu ‘Abd ar-Rahman ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving zakat, the pilgrimage to the House, and fasting Ramadan.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم -وَهُوَ الصَّادِقُ الْمَصْدُوقُ-: إنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ يُجْمَعُ خَلْقُهُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا نُطْفَةً، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ عَلَقَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ مُضْغَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يُرْسَلُ إلَيْهِ الْمَلَكُ فَيَنْفُخُ فِيهِ الرُّوحَ، وَيُؤْمَرُ بِأَرْبَعِ كَلِمَاتٍ: بِكَتْبِ رِزْقِهِ، وَأَجَلِهِ، وَعَمَلِهِ، وَشَقِيٍّ أَمْ سَعِيدٍ؛ فَوَاَللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا إلَهَ غَيْرُهُ إنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ حَتَّى مَا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا إلَّا ذِرَاعٌ فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ فَيَدْخُلُهَا. وَإِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ حَتَّى مَا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا إلَّا ذِرَاعٌ فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ فَيَدْخُلُهَا.

s: Al-Bukhari and Muslim report this from ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud, who introduces it with a phrase of unusual weight: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the truthful, the one believed in, told us.” He wanted his listeners to know that what followed was from the one who does not lie and whose report is certain.
m: The hadith describes the stages of the human being in the womb: forty days as a drop (nutfah), forty as a clot (‘alaqah), forty as a lump (mudghah). Then an angel is sent, and the soul is breathed in, and the angel is commanded to write four things: his provision, his term, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy.

The second part is sometimes read in fear and sometimes in comfort. “One of you does the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only an arm’s length between him and it, then the writing overtakes him and he does the deeds of the people of the Fire, and enters it.” Scholars explain that this refers to those whose outward deeds were not sincere, and that a person’s end is according to what is in his heart. And the opposite is also true: a person may do the deeds of the people of the Fire and then be given guidance. This is why believers ask Allah for a good ending (husn al-khatimah).
l: Do not rely on past deeds, and do not despair because of past sins. The end is in Allah’s hands.
Ask Allah for firmness and a good ending every day.
Remember that the decree is not an excuse to stop acting: the angel writes what Allah knows you will do.

en:
On the authority of Abu ‘Abd ar-Rahman ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the truthful, the one whose truthfulness is confirmed, told us: “Each of you is brought together in his mother’s womb for forty days as a drop; then he is a clot of blood for a similar period; then a lump of flesh for a similar period. Then the angel is sent to him and breathes the soul into him, and he is commanded to write four things: his provision, his life span, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy.

By Allah, other than Whom there is no god, one of you will do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only an arm’s length between him and it, and then what is written overtakes him, so he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And one of you will do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is only an arm’s length between him and it, and then what is written overtakes him, so he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it.”

ar: عَنْ أُمِّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أُمِّ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا، قَالَتْ: قَالَ: رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم مَنْ أَحْدَثَ فِي أَمْرِنَا هَذَا مَا لَيْسَ مِنْهُ فَهُوَ رَدٌّ، وَفِي رِوَايَةٍ لِمُسْلِمٍ: مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلًا لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْرُنَا فَهُوَ رَدٌّ

s: Al-Bukhari and Muslim report this from ‘A’ishah. Muslim’s wording is broader: “Whoever does an act that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected.” Scholars of hadith say that the second wording makes clear that the rule applies even to someone who did not “introduce” the matter himself but followed it.
m: The hadith is called one of the foundations of Islam in the field of acts of worship, as the first hadith, on intentions, is the measure of the inner side. This one is the measure of the outer. An act of worship needs two things: to be for Allah (sincerity), and to be according to what the Prophet ﷺ brought (following). Without sincerity it is show; without following it is an innovation.

“Rejected” (radd) means it will not be accepted by Allah. Scholars use the hadith to explain the principle that in worship, the basis is to hold to what is established, and in customs and worldly dealings, the basis is permission unless something is forbidden. They distinguish between “innovation” in the language, any new thing, and innovation in the religion, adding to worship what the law did not establish. The scholars have discussed the details of what falls in each category and differ on some cases, but they agree on the principle.
l: Before you adopt a practice as worship, ask: where is it from? Learn from sound sources.
Hold to the Sunnah in the way you pray, fast and remember Allah.
Be gentle with those who differ over details; keep the principle firm.

en:
On the authority of the Mother of the Believers, Umm ‘Abdullah ‘A’ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever introduces into this matter of ours something that is not part of it, it is rejected.”

In a narration of Muslim: “Whoever does an action that our matter does not rest upon, it is rejected.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ النُّعْمَانِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، قَالَ: سَمِعْت رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَقُولُ: إنَّ الْحَلَالَ بَيِّنٌ، وَإِنَّ الْحَرَامَ بَيِّنٌ، وَبَيْنَهُمَا أُمُورٌ مُشْتَبِهَاتٌ لَا يَعْلَمُهُنَّ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ النَّاسِ، فَمَنْ اتَّقَى الشُّبُهَاتِ فَقْد اسْتَبْرَأَ لِدِينِهِ وَعِرْضِهِ، وَمَنْ وَقَعَ فِي الشُّبُهَاتِ وَقَعَ فِي الْحَرَامِ، كَالرَّاعِي يَرْعَى حَوْلَ الْحِمَى يُوشِكُ أَنْ يَرْتَعَ فِيهِ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ لِكُلِّ مَلِكٍ حِمًى، أَلَا وَإِنَّ حِمَى اللَّهِ مَحَارِمُهُ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ فِي الْجَسَدِ مُضْغَةً إذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، وَإذَا فَسَدَتْ فَسَدَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، أَلَا وَهِيَ الْقَلْبُ.

s: Al-Bukhari and Muslim report this from an-Nu‘man ibn Bashir, who is said to have pointed to his ears while narrating it, as if to say that he had heard it himself. He was a child of about eight at the time, which shows the quality of memory in that generation and the care they took in transmission.
m: The structure is a map of the moral world: the clearly lawful; the clearly forbidden; and between them matters that many people do not know. The one who takes care to avoid the doubtful matters has protected his religion (his obligation to Allah) and his honour (his standing among people). The one who falls into them may fall into the forbidden.

The Prophet ﷺ gives the image of a shepherd who grazes his flock near a protected pasture: he is likely to have them stray into it. Every king has a protected land, and the protected land of Allah is what He has forbidden. Then comes the famous ending: “In the body is a piece of flesh. If it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Truly, it is the heart.”
l: Learn the clear rulings so that you can recognise the doubtful ones.
Keep a safe distance from the edge of what is forbidden.
Take care of your heart: it is what everything else obeys.

en: On the authority of Abu ‘Abdillah an-Nu‘man ibn Bashir (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “What is lawful is clear, and what is unlawful is clear, and between the two are doubtful matters which many people do not know. So whoever guards against the doubtful has kept his religion and his honour safe; and whoever falls into the doubtful falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd who grazes his flock around a protected pasture, about to graze in it. Truly every king has a protected pasture, and truly Allah’s protected pasture is what He has forbidden. Truly, in the body there is a piece of flesh: if it is sound the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt the whole body is corrupt. Truly, it is the heart.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي رُقَيَّةَ تَمِيمِ بْنِ أَوْسٍ الدَّارِيِّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ.» قُلْنَا: لِمَنْ؟ قَالَ: «لِلَّهِ، وَلِكِتَابِهِ، وَلِرَسُولِهِ، وَلِأَئِمَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَعَامَّتِهِمْ.»

s: Muslim reports this from Tamim ad-Dari, a Companion of the tribe of Lakhm who had been a Christian before he came to Islam in the year 9 AH. The Prophet ﷺ once told the people a remarkable story he had heard from Tamim, about an island and a creature he met there (it is in Sahih Muslim), which shows how highly he regarded him.
m: “Ad-din an-nasihah.” The word naseehah comes from the idea of purity and sincerity. Its use in Arabic includes the sewing together of a garment and the purification of honey. Scholars explain it as wishing good for the other with sincerity. The Prophet ﷺ repeated the statement three times, then listed to whom it is owed: to Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their common people.

Each has its own form. Naseehah for Allah is sincerity in worship and belief. For His Book, to believe in it, recite it, understand it and act on it. For His Messenger, to believe in him, obey him and love him. For the leaders, to help them in what is right and to advise them privately. For the people, to wish them good, teach them, and not deceive them.
l: Make advising a habit: gentle, private, sincere and well-timed.
Be open to receiving naseehah from others.
Let your honest effort in work and in family be seen as naseehah.

en: On the authority of Abu Ruqayyah Tamim ibn Aws ad-Dari (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet ﷺ said: “The religion is sincere advice (naseehah).” We said: “For whom?” He said: “For Allah, for His Book, for His Messenger, and for the leaders of the Muslims and their common people.”

ar: عَنْ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَشْهَدُوا أَنْ لَا إلَهَ إلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ، وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ؛ فَإِذَا فَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ عَصَمُوا مِنِّي دِمَاءَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ إلَّا بِحَقِّ الْإِسْلَامِ، وَحِسَابُهُمْ عَلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى.

s: Al-Bukhari and Muslim report this from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar. It is better understood with the discussion that followed the death of the Prophet ﷺ. When some of the Arab tribes refused to pay zakat, ‘Umar questioned Abu Bakr’s decision to fight them, quoting this hadith. Abu Bakr replied, “By Allah, I will fight anyone who separates the prayer from the zakat, for zakat is the right of wealth. By Allah, if they withhold from me a rope that they used to give to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I will fight them for it.” ‘Umar said afterwards, “I saw that Allah had opened Abu Bakr’s heart to fight, and I knew it was the truth” (al-Bukhari and Muslim).
m: The hadith needs to be read with its context and with the rest of the texts. The Qur’an states, “There is no compulsion in religion” (2:256), and the Prophet ﷺ made covenants with those who did not believe. Scholars explain that the hadith is about the idolaters of Arabia who were at war with the Muslims: when they entered Islam by their own choice, their lives and property were protected. It is not an instruction to force people to believe, nor does it apply to those under treaty or to peaceful non-Muslims, whose lives and property are protected by Islamic law.

For the person who has entered Islam, outward conduct is what the law takes into account: “their reckoning is with Allah”. The state judges by what appears and does not search hearts. This is why the hadith protects the lives and wealth of those who say the shahadah.
l: Do not accuse another Muslim of hypocrisy on suspicion. Judging hearts is for Allah.
Remember that the right of wealth, zakat, is as binding as prayer.
Read hadith with their context and in light of the whole of the religion.

en: On the authority of Ibn ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and establish the prayer and give zakat. If they do that, their blood and their property are protected from me, except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning is with Allah the Exalted.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ صَخْرٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: سَمِعْت رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَقُولُ: مَا نَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْهُ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ، وَمَا أَمَرْتُكُمْ بِهِ فَأْتُوا مِنْهُ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ، فَإِنَّمَا أَهْلَكَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ كَثْرَةُ مَسَائِلِهِمْ وَاخْتِلَافُهُمْ عَلَى أَنْبِيَائِهِمْ.

s: Al-Bukhari and Muslim report this from Abu Hurayrah. Muslim records its occasion: the Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon and said, “O people, Allah has made the Hajj obligatory upon you, so perform Hajj.” A man asked, “Is it every year, O Messenger of Allah?” He was silent, and the man repeated it three times. Then the Prophet ﷺ said, “If I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and you would not have been able to do it. Leave me as I leave you. Those before you were destroyed by their many questions and their disagreements with their prophets.”
m: The three instructions are all in this one hadith: whatever I forbade you, avoid; whatever I commanded you, do as much as you are able; and do not burden yourselves with questions that are not needed. The difference between them is notable. The prohibition is to be avoided entirely, because leaving something is always possible. The command is to be done to the extent of capacity.

Scholars have drawn on this hadith for the principle that hardship brings ease, and that “the matter is according to ability”. It is also a lesson on how to ask. Asking in order to learn what you need is a duty. Asking for the sake of trouble, or to find the limit of what is required, can bring burdens. The Qur’an also advises against questions that “if shown to you, would distress you” (5:101).
l: Avoid every forbidden thing completely, and do what you can of the commands.
Ask when you need to know, and do not be a person who searches for loopholes.
Take the religion as it came, with its ease.

en: On the authority of Abu Hurayrah ‘Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sakhr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “What I have forbidden you, avoid; and what I have commanded you, do as much of it as you are able. For what destroyed those before you was only their excessive questioning and their disagreeing with their prophets.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم «إنَّ اللَّهَ طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إلَّا طَيِّبًا، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ أَمَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِمَا أَمَرَ بِهِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ فَقَالَ تَعَالَى: «يَا أَيُّهَا الرُّسُلُ كُلُوا مِنْ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَاعْمَلُوا صَالِحًا»، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: «يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ» ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ الرَّجُلَ يُطِيلُ السَّفَرَ أَشْعَثَ أَغْبَرَ يَمُدُّ يَدَيْهِ إلَى السَّمَاءِ: يَا رَبِّ! يَا رَبِّ! وَمَطْعَمُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَمَشْرَبُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَمَلْبَسُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَغُذِّيَ بِالْحَرَامِ، فَأَنَّى يُسْتَجَابُ لَهُ؟».

s: Muslim reports this from Abu Hurayrah. It begins with two verses. “O messengers, eat from the good things and do righteous deeds” (23:51), and “O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided for you” (2:172). The Prophet ﷺ then spoke of a man, and the picture he draws is one of the most striking in the whole of the hadith literature.
m: The man is a traveller, dishevelled and dusty, who is making a long journey: the circumstances in which du‘a is most likely to be answered. He raises his hands to the sky and says, “O Lord! O Lord!” But his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with the unlawful. “So how can he be answered?” The Prophet ﷺ is describing every condition that normally brings acceptance, and then pointing to the one thing that blocks it.

Scholars explain that “Allah is pure (tayyib)” means that He is free of every deficiency, and therefore accepts only what is pure: pure in its source, and also sincere in its intention. The hadith ties the lawfulness of what a person earns and consumes to the acceptance of his worship, in particular his supplication. It is not meant to cause despair, but to remind us that the cure is within reach: purify income, and turn back.
l: Look at the sources of your income, your food and your clothing: are they clean?
If you have wronged someone in a transaction, return what is due before you ask Allah for anything.
Make the lawful the basis of your life, as the verse says to the messengers.

en: On the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah is Good and accepts only what is good. Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers. He the Exalted said: ‘O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds’; and He the Exalted said: ‘O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided for you.’” Then he mentioned a man who travels far, dishevelled and dusty, stretching his hands to the sky: “O Lord! O Lord!”, while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with the unlawful. “So how can he be answered?”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ سِبْطِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم وَرَيْحَانَتِهِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، قَالَ: حَفِظْت مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم دَعْ مَا يُرِيبُك إلَى مَا لَا يُرِيبُك.

s: At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa’i report this from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali, the Prophet’s grandson, who memorised it as a child. Al-Hasan was only about seven or eight years old when the Prophet ﷺ died, which gives an idea of the quality of the instruction these children received. He is also the one to whom the Prophet ﷺ taught the du‘a of qunut in the witr prayer, “Allahumma ihdini fiman hadayt...” (Abu Dawud and others).
m: “Da‘ ma yuribuka ila ma la yuribuka”: leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt. Yuribu is from rayb: uneasiness, a disturbance in the heart. The principle is simple: where there are two options, one certain and one doubtful, take the certain.

The Prophet ﷺ gives a reason that is about the heart: “truthfulness is tranquillity and falsehood is doubt.” The truth settles the heart; a lie leaves it uneasy. A person who is sincere will feel that unease, and the hadith asks him to trust it, when it concerns what is doubtful in terms of lawful and unlawful. The scholars note that this applies to genuine doubt, not to baseless scruples, which have to be set aside.
l: When something bothers your conscience, step back and examine it before you proceed.
In money matters, choose the clear over the unclear.
Do not allow obsessive doubts to run your life: this hadith is about genuine unease.

en: On the authority of Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, the grandson of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his beloved (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: I memorised from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم مِنْ حُسْنِ إسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ.

s: At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah report this from Abu Hurayrah, and it is graded hasan. It is among the shortest of the Prophet’s comprehensive sayings, the jawami‘ al-kalim, and early scholars said that it alone is enough to organise a person’s manners.
m: “Part of the excellence of a person’s Islam is that he leaves what does not concern him.” The things that do not concern him are what has no benefit for his religion or his worldly good: idle talk, prying into other people’s business, arguments with no purpose, looking at what is of no use. The word is “ya‘nihi”: what concerns or matters to him.

The saying is not asking for withdrawal from society. What concerns a person includes his duties to his family, community and Muslims at large. It says that attention is limited, and that a person’s Islam is made better when his attention is spent on what is useful. This is a comfort too: you are not responsible for everything.
l: Ask yourself before speaking or acting: does this matter to my religion or my life?
Spend less time on gossip, news you cannot act upon, and arguments that do not end.
Give your attention to your duties and your growth.

en: On the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Part of the excellence of a person’s Islam is his leaving alone what does not concern him.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ خَادِمِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ.

s: Al-Bukhari and Muslim report this from Anas ibn Malik. Muslim’s version adds “or for his neighbour”: “None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother, or for his neighbour, what he loves for himself.” Anas, who served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years, heard it as the key to relationships.
m: The standard is demanding and clear: use yourself as the measure. What do you want for yourself? Safety, success, respect, forgiveness, guidance, a good life. Then want these same things for your brother. The negative side is also included: you do not like to be cheated or insulted or have your faults spread, so do not do these to others.

The hadith negates faith, in the sense of its completeness: “none of you believes” means that your faith is not complete. Scholars say that this love is of the heart, not just of conduct: it excludes envy, which is the opposite. The Companions put it into practice. The Ansar of Madinah, for example, shared their homes and orchards with the Muhajirun, as the Qur’an praises: “They give them preference over themselves, even though they are in need” (59:9).
l: When you succeed, wish the same for your colleague. When you give a gift, wish that they would give you good too.
Treat envy as a sickness of the heart and ask Allah to heal it.
Apply the mirror: before you act toward someone, ask how you would feel in their place.

en: On the authority of Abu Hamzah Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.”

ar: عَنْ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم لَا يَحِلُّ دَمُ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ [ يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأني رسول الله] إلَّا بِإِحْدَى ثَلَاثٍ: الثَّيِّبُ الزَّانِي، وَالنَّفْسُ بِالنَّفْسِ، وَالتَّارِكُ لِدِينِهِ الْمُفَارِقُ لِلْجَمَاعَةِ.

s: Al-Bukhari and Muslim report this from ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud. It states the sanctity of the blood of a Muslim, one of the most strongly protected rights in the religion, and then names three narrow exceptions. In the Farewell Sermon the Prophet ﷺ said that the blood, wealth and honour of Muslims are as sacred as that day, in that month, in that land (al-Bukhari and Muslim).
m: The three: a married person who commits adultery, a life for a life (retaliation for murder), and the one who abandons his religion and separates from the community. Scholars of the law are firm on two points. First, these are matters for the courts and legal authority, with the proper conditions of proof and procedure, not for individuals to carry out. Second, the penalties are narrow: they are linked to proof, to the judge, and to the possibility of mercy and repentance.

The weight of the hadith is in its opening. A Muslim’s blood is sacred, and any threat to a life is a serious matter: the Qur’an equates killing one innocent soul with killing all humankind (5:32). It is a call to the greatest care in speech and action regarding life.
l: Never treat a human life lightly, in words or in deeds.
Leave legal matters to those who are qualified and authorised.
Be among the people who are a source of safety.

en: On the authority of Ibn Mas‘ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The blood of a Muslim, one who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, is not lawful except in one of three cases: a married person who commits adultery, a life for a life, and one who leaves his religion and separates from the community.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ جَارَهُ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ ضَيْفَهُ.

s: Al-Bukhari and Muslim report this from Abu Hurayrah. Its three parts are three obligations that stand on faith in Allah and the Last Day: speak well or be silent; honour your neighbour; honour your guest. The wording puts faith as the root and conduct as the fruit.
m: “Let him speak good or keep silent.” Imam ash-Shafi‘i is reported to have explained that when a person wants to speak, he should think first: if there is no harm in what he will say, he may speak; if there is doubt, he should refrain. The point is that speech is an act that will be accounted for. The Qur’an says that no word is uttered without a watcher ready (50:18).

The neighbour and the guest follow. Honouring the guest includes a warm welcome, the best of what one has, and keeping to the period of hospitality that the Prophet ﷺ described as three days, with the first day as his special entertainment (al-Bukhari and Muslim). The guest, in turn, should not stay so long that he becomes a burden.
l: Before sending a message or answering back, ask: is this good? Is it necessary? If not, be silent.
Welcome guests with the best you have, and with a warm face.
Greet your neighbour and ask about their wellbeing.

en: On the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent; and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his neighbour; and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his guest.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ رَجُلًا قَالَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم أَوْصِنِي. قَالَ: لَا تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لَا تَغْضَبْ «.

s: Al-Bukhari reports this from Abu Hurayrah. A man said to the Prophet ﷺ, “Advise me.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time the Prophet ﷺ answered, “Do not become angry.”
m: That the Prophet ﷺ gave a whole life’s counsel in two words suggests either that this man’s own weakness was anger, or that anger is the root of many other evils. Scholars consider that the Prophet ﷺ answers each questioner according to what is most needed, and that anger is a gate through which much harm passes: broken relationships, harsh words, blows, regret.

The command is read in two ways. One is to avoid the causes of anger: arrogance, hurry, showing off, too many arguments. The other is to control it when it comes: not to carry out what it urges. The hadith on real strength says the strong one is the one who controls himself in anger. And the remedies are in the Sunnah: say “A‘udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim”, change position (if standing, sit; if sitting, lie down), make wudu, and keep silent.
l: Learn your own triggers, and plan what you will do before the anger arrives.
Use the remedies: refuge in Allah, silence, sitting, wudu.
When you are angry, delay your reply until it has passed.

en: On the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): A man said to the Prophet ﷺ, “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he said: “Do not become angry.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي يَعْلَى شَدَّادِ بْنِ أَوْسٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الْإِحْسَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، فَإِذَا قَتَلْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا الْقِتْلَةَ، وَإِذَا ذَبَحْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا الذِّبْحَةَ، وَلْيُحِدَّ أَحَدُكُمْ شَفْرَتَهُ، وَلْيُرِحْ ذَبِيحَتَهُ.

s: Muslim reports this from Shaddad ibn Aws, a Companion of the Ansar who was known for his forbearance and knowledge. The sentence comes at the beginning of a statement about the slaughter of animals, and so it reminds us that the Prophet ﷺ discussed how even a necessary act should be done.
m: “Allah has prescribed excellence (ihsan) in everything.” Ihsan means doing a thing in the best way possible, with care and good intention. The Prophet ﷺ then gives examples that are deliberately hard: “If you kill, kill well; if you slaughter, slaughter well. Let one of you sharpen his blade and give the animal rest.” Even in the case of killing, which is sometimes necessary, there is a manner. Scholars add from other reports that the knife should be sharpened away from the animal, and that one animal should not be made to watch another being slaughtered.

If this is the care owed to an animal, what is owed to human beings? Scholars see the hadith as laying the principle of ihsan over all work: do it with quality. The work of a craftsman, a teacher, a cook, a doctor: all of it is to be done with excellence, as it is an act in the sight of Allah.
l: Choose one task today and do it with extra care, as an act of worship.
Be gentle with animals, in keeping and in slaughter.
Let ihsan be the standard of your work: not what will pass, but what is excellent.

en: On the authority of Abu Ya‘la Shaddad ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: “Truly Allah has prescribed excellence (ihsan) in everything. So when you kill, kill well; and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let each of you sharpen his blade and let him spare the animal pain.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ جُنْدَبِ بْنِ جُنَادَةَ، وَأَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ مُعَاذِ بْنِ جَبَلٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْت، وَأَتْبِعْ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقْ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ.

s: At-Tirmidhi reports this from Abu Dharr, and it is graded hasan. Imam Ahmad has it from Mu‘adh ibn Jabal, in a narration that places the advice at the time he was sent to teach in Yemen. It has a familiar form: three short instructions, each enough to shape a life.
m: The first is taqwa “wherever you are”: Allah is aware of you in every place, in public and in private, so that your behaviour does not vary with who is watching. The second is that a good deed follows a bad deed to erase it, which the Qur’an confirms: “Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds” (11:114). The third is to treat people with good character.

The order is instructive. Between you and Allah there is taqwa and there is repair, since you will err. Between you and people is good character. The scholars noticed that the hadith places the duty to Allah and the duty to people together, as the Prophet ﷺ did so often, as two parts of the same excellence.
l: Behave in private as you would in public.
After a sin, do a good deed quickly: a prayer, a charity, a kind word.
Take care of your manners with people as part of your worship.

en: On the authority of Abu Dharr Jundub ibn Junadah and Abu ‘Abd ar-Rahman Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: “Fear Allah wherever you are; follow up a bad deed with a good one and it will wipe it out; and treat people with good character.”

ar: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: «كُنْت خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَوْمًا، فَقَالَ: يَا غُلَامِ! إنِّي أُعَلِّمُك كَلِمَاتٍ: احْفَظْ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْك، احْفَظْ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَك، إذَا سَأَلْت فَاسْأَلْ اللَّهَ، وَإِذَا اسْتَعَنْت فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاَللَّهِ، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْأُمَّةَ لَوْ اجْتَمَعَتْ عَلَى أَنْ يَنْفَعُوك بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَنْفَعُوك إلَّا بِشَيْءٍ قَدْ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ لَك، وَإِنْ اجْتَمَعُوا عَلَى أَنْ يَضُرُّوك بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَضُرُّوك إلَّا بِشَيْءٍ قَدْ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْك؛ رُفِعَتْ الْأَقْلَامُ، وَجَفَّتْ الصُّحُفُ». وَفِي رِوَايَةِ غَيْرِ التِّرْمِذِيِّ: «احْفَظْ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ أمامك، تَعَرَّفْ إلَى اللَّهِ فِي الرَّخَاءِ يَعْرِفُك فِي الشِّدَّةِ، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ مَا أَخْطَأَك لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُصِيبَك، وَمَا أَصَابَك لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُخْطِئَك، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ النَّصْرَ مَعَ الصَّبْرِ، وَأَنْ الْفَرَجَ مَعَ الْكَرْبِ، وَأَنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا

s: At-Tirmidhi reports this from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, and grades it hasan sahih. Ibn ‘Abbas was a boy at the time, about ten years old, riding behind the Prophet ﷺ on his mount. “One day I was behind the Prophet ﷺ,” he said, “and he said, ‘Young man, I will teach you some words.’” The intimacy of the scene is part of its power: a child on the back of the animal, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turning to him to teach him what would be needed for life.
m: “Guard Allah and He will guard you.” To guard Allah is to guard His limits and His rights, His commands and prohibitions. Allah’s guarding in return is a protection in body, family, religion and in the Hereafter. “Guard Allah and you will find Him before you”: His support will be present.

Then: “When you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek help from Allah.” The believer uses means and works with people, but his reliance is on Allah alone. “Know that if the whole community were to gather to benefit you, they could benefit you only with what Allah has already written for you; and if they gathered to harm you, they could harm you only with what Allah has written.” The hadith ends with a line of great finality: “The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.” What was decreed is written; what remains is how we respond.
l: Hold to Allah’s limits in private, and expect His protection in return.
Bring your needs to Him before you bring them to people.
Let go of fear of what people may do. Allah has the matter in His hand.

en:
On the authority of ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: One day I was behind the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Young man, I will teach you some words. Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the whole nation were to gather to benefit you with something, they could benefit you only with what Allah has already written for you; and if they were to gather to harm you with something, they could harm you only with what Allah has already written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.”

In a narration other than at-Tirmidhi: “Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. Get to know Allah in times of ease and He will know you in times of hardship. Know that what missed you was never going to befall you, and what befell you was never going to miss you. Know that victory comes with patience, relief comes with distress, and with hardship there is ease.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي مَسْعُودٍ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ عَمْرٍو الْأَنْصَارِيِّ الْبَدْرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم إنَّ مِمَّا أَدْرَكَ النَّاسُ مِنْ كَلَامِ النُّبُوَّةِ الْأُولَى: إذَا لَمْ تَسْتَحِ فَاصْنَعْ مَا شِئْت.

s: Al-Bukhari reports this from Abu Mas‘ud ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amr al-Badri, a Companion of the Ansar who was present at the pledge of ‘Aqabah and lived in Kufa. The Prophet ﷺ framed it as an inheritance: “Among what people have received from the words of the earliest prophethood is: if you feel no shame, do as you wish.” It is a sentence that has passed from prophet to prophet and has remained alive among people.
m: The words can be read in two ways, and the scholars mention both. The first reading takes the command as a warning in the form of a command, like the verse “Do as you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do” (41:40). A person who has no shame, no inner restraint, will do whatever he wants, and the consequence is on him. The second reading takes it as a permission: if what you are about to do is such that you would not be ashamed of it before Allah and people, then do it.

Both readings place shame (haya’) at the centre of morality. It is the internal guard that prevents wrong before the law does. The Prophet ﷺ said in another narration, “Shame is part of faith” and “Shame brings nothing but good”. The one who has lost it has lost the one brake that is always with him.
l: Cultivate shame before Allah: ask “would I be comfortable if this were shown to Him and to people?”
Admire and protect it in children; do not mock a child for blushing.
Avoid environments that wear down your sense of shame.

en: On the authority of Abu Mas‘ud ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amr al-Ansari al-Badri (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Among what people have learned from the words of the earlier prophecy is: If you feel no shame, do as you wish.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي عَمْرٍو وَقِيلَ: أَبِي عَمْرَةَ سُفْيَانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قُلْت: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ! قُلْ لِي فِي الْإِسْلَامِ قَوْلًا لَا أَسْأَلُ عَنْهُ أَحَدًا غَيْرَك؛ قَالَ: قُلْ: آمَنْت بِاَللَّهِ ثُمَّ اسْتَقِمْ.

s: Muslim reports this from Abu ‘Amr (or Abu ‘Amrah) Sufyan ibn ‘Abdillah ath-Thaqafi, a Companion from Ta’if. He asked the Prophet ﷺ for a statement about Islam that would leave him in no need of asking anyone else after the Prophet. The answer was one line.
At-Tirmidhi preserves a follow-up: Sufyan asked, “What do you fear most for me?” and the Prophet ﷺ took hold of his own tongue and said, “This.”
m: “Say: I believe in Allah, then be upright.” It has two parts. The first is a statement of faith, made with the tongue and the heart. The second is steadfastness (istiqamah): to remain on the straight path, in belief and conduct, without deviating to either side. It echoes the verse “Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is Allah,’ and then remain on a right course, the angels will descend upon them: ‘Do not fear and do not grieve’” (41:30).

Istiqamah is harder than the first step. Abu Bakr is reported to have been asked what it means and to have answered that it is not to associate anything with Allah. ‘Umar said that it is to hold to command and prohibition and not to twist away like the fox. The Prophet ﷺ said elsewhere, “Be upright, though you will not be able to count it all” (Ibn Majah): it is to be sought as far as possible, with repentance for falling short.
l: Say it, and live it: let the declaration lead you to repeated, small acts of obedience.
Be steady rather than spectacular, and return when you slip.
Guard your tongue, because it is the part most likely to take you off the path.

en: On the authority of Abu ‘Amr, and it is also said Abu ‘Amrah, Sufyan ibn ‘Abdillah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me something about Islam that I could ask no one else about but you.” He said: “Say: I believe in Allah; and then be steadfast.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: أَنَّ رَجُلًا سَأَلَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم فَقَالَ: أَرَأَيْت إذَا صَلَّيْت الْمَكْتُوبَاتِ، وَصُمْت رَمَضَانَ، وَأَحْلَلْت الْحَلَالَ، وَحَرَّمْت الْحَرَامَ، وَلَمْ أَزِدْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ شَيْئًا؛ أَأَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ.

s: Muslim reports this from Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah. A man, named in some narrations as an-Nu‘man ibn Qawqal, asked the Prophet ﷺ, “Do you think that if I pray the obligatory prayers, fast Ramadan, treat the lawful as lawful and the unlawful as unlawful, and add nothing to that, I will enter Paradise?” The Prophet ﷺ said, “Yes.” The man said, “By Allah, I will add nothing to it.”
m: It is a question that is practical in a good way: what is the least that I must do, and will it be enough? The Prophet ﷺ’s answer shows that the obligations suffice for entry, when joined by the right attitude toward the lawful and unlawful. “Treating the lawful as lawful” means to believe in it and act upon it; “the unlawful as unlawful” is to avoid it and not to make it permissible.

Scholars say that the man’s statement “I will add nothing” does not mean he would neglect voluntary deeds: it refers to not adding new obligations. The obligatory is the foundation, and it was for the Prophet ﷺ himself to say whether a man would be saved. The voluntary deeds make up for shortfalls in the obligatory ones, as another hadith states.
l: Make sure that the obligatory acts are in place and sound before you add more.
Do not call lawful what Allah has called unlawful, or the reverse.
Add voluntary worship, since it completes what is lacking.

en: On the authority of Abu ‘Abdillah Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with them both): A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, “Tell me: if I pray the obligatory prayers, fast Ramadan, treat as lawful what is lawful and as unlawful what is unlawful, and add nothing to that, will I enter Paradise?” He said: “Yes.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي مَالِكٍ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ عَاصِمٍ الْأَشْعَرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم الطَّهُورُ شَطْرُ الْإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلَأُ الْمِيزَانَ، وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلَآنِ -أَوْ: تَمْلَأُ- مَا بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ، وَالصَّدَقَةُ بُرْهَانٌ، وَالصَّبْرُ ضِيَاءٌ، وَالْقُرْآنُ حُجَّةٌ لَك أَوْ عَلَيْك، كُلُّ النَّاسِ يَغْدُو، فَبَائِعٌ نَفْسَهُ فَمُعْتِقُهَا أَوْ مُوبِقُهَا.

s: Muslim reports this from Abu Malik al-Harith ibn ‘Asim al-Ash‘ari. It is a short lecture in seven lines, with each line an image. The ending turns the images back on the listener.
m: “Purity is half of faith”: whether this means that cleanliness is itself half of the full religion, or that faith has two parts, leaving the impure and adopting the pure, the idea is that the clean life is a matter of belief. “Al-hamdulillah fills the scale”: a single word of praise, sincerely said, carries so much weight that it fills the balance of deeds.

“Prayer is light” (nur): light on the face, in the heart, in the grave and on the Day of Resurrection. “Charity is proof” (burhan): evidence that the heart believes, since giving is hard for the self and shows what one prefers. “Patience is illumination” (diya’): a light that has heat in it, as sun does: patience on obedience, away from sin and in trials, is hard and brings brightness. “The Qur’an is a proof for you or against you.” Then the last line: “Everyone goes out in the morning and sells himself, either setting himself free or bringing about his ruin.”
l: Say alhamdulillah when you wake, and mean it.
Pick one of the seven and work on it for a week.
Each morning, ask: with what am I selling myself today?

en: On the authority of Abu Malik al-Harith ibn ‘Asim al-Ash‘ari (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Purity is half of faith. ‘Alhamdu lillah’ fills the scale; ‘Subhan Allah wal-hamdu lillah’ fill what is between the heavens and the earth. Prayer is light, charity is a proof, patience is illumination, and the Qur’an is an argument for you or against you. Everyone goes out in the morning and sells himself, either freeing himself or destroying himself.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ الْغِفَارِيِّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم فِيمَا يَرْوِيهِ عَنْ رَبِّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: يَا عِبَادِي: إنِّي حَرَّمْت الظُّلْمَ عَلَى نَفْسِي، وَجَعَلْته بَيْنَكُمْ مُحَرَّمًا؛ فَلَا تَظَالَمُوا. يَا عِبَادِي! كُلُّكُمْ ضَالٌّ إلَّا مَنْ هَدَيْته، فَاسْتَهْدُونِي أَهْدِكُمْ. يَا عِبَادِي! كُلُّكُمْ جَائِعٌ إلَّا مَنْ أَطْعَمْته، فَاسْتَطْعِمُونِي أُطْعِمْكُمْ. يَا عِبَادِي! كُلُّكُمْ عَارٍ إلَّا مَنْ كَسَوْته، فَاسْتَكْسُونِي أَكْسُكُمْ. يَا عِبَادِي! إنَّكُمْ تُخْطِئُونَ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ، وَأَنَا أَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا؛ فَاسْتَغْفِرُونِي أَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ. يَا عِبَادِي! إنَّكُمْ لَنْ تَبْلُغُوا ضُرِّي فَتَضُرُّونِي، وَلَنْ تَبْلُغُوا نَفْعِي فَتَنْفَعُونِي. يَا عِبَادِي! لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ كَانُوا عَلَى أَتْقَى قَلْبِ رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ مِنْكُمْ، مَا زَادَ ذَلِكَ فِي مُلْكِي شَيْئًا. يَا عِبَادِي! لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ كَانُوا عَلَى أَفْجَرِ قَلْبِ رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ مِنْكُمْ، مَا نَقَصَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ مُلْكِي شَيْئًا. يَا عِبَادِي! لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ قَامُوا فِي صَعِيدٍ وَاحِدٍ، فَسَأَلُونِي، فَأَعْطَيْت كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مَسْأَلَته، مَا نَقَصَ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا عِنْدِي إلَّا كَمَا يَنْقُصُ الْمِخْيَطُ إذَا أُدْخِلَ الْبَحْرَ. يَا عِبَادِي! إنَّمَا هِيَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ أُحْصِيهَا لَكُمْ، ثُمَّ أُوَفِّيكُمْ إيَّاهَا؛ فَمَنْ وَجَدَ خَيْرًا فَلْيَحْمَدْ اللَّهَ، وَمَنْ وَجَدَ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ فَلَا يَلُومَن إلَّا نَفْسَهُ.

s: Muslim reports this long hadith qudsi from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, who is said to have taken it from the Prophet ﷺ’s words about his Lord. Abu Idris al-Khawlani, one of the great scholars of Damascus and a narrator of the hadith, is reported to have knelt on his knees whenever he told it, out of respect for its weight. It is among the noblest texts in the whole collection.
m: It starts with a prohibition by Allah on Himself: “I have forbidden oppression for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not oppress one another.” Then it moves through a series of statements about human need. “All of you are astray except those I guide, so seek guidance from Me.” “All of you are hungry except those I feed, so ask Me for food.” “All of you are naked except those I clothe.” Each time the pattern is need, and the instruction to ask. We have nothing except what He gives.

Then the scale of Allah’s independence: if the first of you and the last of you, human and jinn, were as pious as the most pious heart among you, it would add nothing to His dominion; if they were as wicked as the most wicked heart, it would take nothing from it. The needle simile: if they all asked Him and He gave each what he asked, it would reduce what He has no more than a needle reduces the sea when dipped in it. And the final reckoning: “It is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay you for. Whoever finds good, let him praise Allah; whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.”
l: Ask Allah for everything, including what seems small: food, guidance, clothing, forgiveness.
Remember that your worship is for your own benefit, as He has no need of it.
When you find good, thank Allah. When you fall short, look to yourself.

en:
On the authority of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, in what he relates from his Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, that He said: “O My servants, I have forbidden oppression for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not oppress one another.

O My servants, all of you are astray except those I guide, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except those I feed, so ask Me for food and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except those I clothe, so ask Me for clothing and I will clothe you.

O My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so ask Me for forgiveness and I will forgive you. O My servants, you will never reach harming Me so as to harm Me, and you will never reach benefiting Me so as to benefit Me.

O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, were all as pious as the most pious heart of any one man among you, that would add nothing to My kingdom. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, were all as wicked as the most wicked heart of any one man among you, that would take nothing from My kingdom.

O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, were to stand in one place and ask of Me, and I gave every one of them what he asked, that would reduce what I have no more than a needle reduces the sea when it is put into it.

O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay you for. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah; and whoever finds other than that, let him blame no one but himself.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَيْضًا، أَنَّ نَاسًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالُوا لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ذَهَبَ أَهْلُ الدُّثُورِ بِالْأُجُورِ؛ يُصَلُّونَ كَمَا نُصَلِّي، وَيَصُومُونَ كَمَا نَصُومُ، وَيَتَصَدَّقُونَ بِفُضُولِ أَمْوَالِهِمْ. قَالَ: أَوَلَيْسَ قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ مَا تَصَّدَّقُونَ؟ إنَّ بِكُلِّ تَسْبِيحَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَكُلِّ تَكْبِيرَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَكُلِّ تَحْمِيدَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَكُلِّ تَهْلِيلَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَأَمْرٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ صَدَقَةٌ، وَنَهْيٌ عَنْ مُنْكَرٍ صَدَقَةٌ، وَفِي بُضْعِ أَحَدِكُمْ صَدَقَةٌ. قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَيَأْتِي أَحَدُنَا شَهْوَتَهُ وَيَكُونُ لَهُ فِيهَا أَجْرٌ؟ قَالَ: أَرَأَيْتُمْ لَوْ وَضَعَهَا فِي حَرَامٍ أَكَانَ عَلَيْهِ وِزْرٌ؟ فَكَذَلِكَ إذَا وَضَعَهَا فِي الْحَلَالِ، كَانَ لَهُ أَجْرٌ.

s: Muslim reports this from Abu Dharr. Some of the Companions came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the wealthy have gone off with the rewards: they pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, and they give charity from the surplus of their wealth.” The Prophet ﷺ replied, “Has Allah not given you what you can give in charity? Every tasbih is a charity, every takbir is a charity, every tahmid is a charity, every tahlil is a charity, enjoining good is a charity and forbidding evil is a charity.”
m: Then comes the sentence that surprised the Companions: “and in the intimate relation of one of you with his wife there is charity.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, does one of us satisfy his desire and have a reward in it?” He said, “Tell me, if he did it in what is unlawful, would he not bear a sin? Likewise, if he does it in what is lawful, he has a reward.” This is a statement that ordinary lawful pleasures, done with the right intention, are counted as acts of worship.

The hadith redefines what it means to give. Charity is not limited to wealth: it includes the remembrance of Allah, speech that guides, and the fulfilment of permitted needs with gratitude and the purpose of keeping oneself chaste.
l: Count your dhikr as charity and do not envy the wealthy.
Intend good in what is lawful: eating, marriage, rest, to strengthen yourself for worship.
Enjoin good and forbid evil with wisdom and gentleness.

en: On the authority of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) also: Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Prophet ﷺ, “O Messenger of Allah, the wealthy have gone off with the rewards: they pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, and they give charity from their surplus wealth.” He said: “Has Allah not given you things to give in charity? Every glorification (tasbihah) is a charity, every takbir is a charity, every praise (tahmidah) is a charity, every tahlil is a charity; enjoining good is a charity, forbidding evil is a charity, and in the intimacy of each of you there is a charity.” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, will one of us satisfy his desire and have a reward in it?” He said: “Tell me, if he were to place it in what is unlawful, would he bear a sin? So likewise, if he places it in what is lawful, he will have a reward.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم كُلُّ سُلَامَى مِنْ النَّاسِ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةٌ، كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَطْلُعُ فِيهِ الشَّمْسُ تَعْدِلُ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَتُعِينُ الرَّجُلَ فِي دَابَّتِهِ فَتَحْمِلُهُ عَلَيْهَا أَوْ تَرْفَعُ لَهُ عَلَيْهَا مَتَاعَهُ صَدَقَةٌ، وَالْكَلِمَةُ الطَّيِّبَةُ صَدَقَةٌ، وَبِكُلِّ خُطْوَةٍ تَمْشِيهَا إلَى الصَّلَاةِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَتُمِيطُ الْأَذَى عَنْ الطَّرِيقِ صَدَقَةٌ.

s: Al-Bukhari and Muslim report this from Abu Hurayrah, and Muslim has the explanation from ‘A’ishah: every human being is created with three hundred and sixty joints, and the Prophet ﷺ said that for each joint a charity is owed each day. The words may be understood as a statement of gratitude: the body is a series of joints that work, every one of them a blessing.
m: The examples show how many ordinary actions can be gratitude. “Judging justly between two people”: a mediator, a parent, a neighbour who settles a dispute; “helping a man with his mount”, in our age, with a vehicle or load; “a good word”, which costs nothing and eases a heart; “every step toward the prayer”, which is counted; “removing harm from the road”, an act of care for strangers.

Scholars add the report in Muslim that two rak‘ahs of duha are enough to cover the charities owed from every joint. The wide range of things that are counted ensures that no one is shut out of charity by lack of money.
l: Keep a short list of five easy charities for each day and do them.
Pray duha when you can: it is a daily payment of thanks.
Be the person who settles quarrels and clears the way for others.

en: On the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Every joint of a person owes a charity every day the sun rises: to judge justly between two people is a charity; to help a man with his mount, lifting him onto it or lifting his belongings onto it, is a charity; a good word is a charity; every step you take towards the prayer is a charity; and removing something harmful from the road is a charity.”

ar: عَنْ النَّوَّاسِ بْنِ سَمْعَانَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: «الْبِرُّ حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ، وَالْإِثْمُ مَا حَاكَ فِي صَدْرِك، وَكَرِهْت أَنْ يَطَّلِعَ عَلَيْهِ النَّاسُ». وَعَنْ وَابِصَةَ بْنِ مَعْبَدٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: أَتَيْت رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم فَقَالَ: «جِئْتَ تَسْأَلُ عَنْ الْبِرِّ؟ قُلْت: نَعَمْ. فقَالَ: استفت قلبك، الْبِرُّ مَا اطْمَأَنَّتْ إلَيْهِ النَّفْسُ، وَاطْمَأَنَّ إلَيْهِ الْقَلْبُ، وَالْإِثْمُ مَا حَاكَ فِي النَّفْسِ وَتَرَدَّدَ فِي الصَّدْرِ، وَإِنْ أَفْتَاك النَّاسُ وَأَفْتَوْك».

s: Muslim reports this from an-Nawwas ibn Sam‘an al-Ansari. He said, “I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about righteousness (birr) and sin (ithm).” Another narration, in Ahmad and ad-Darimi, from Wabisah ibn Ma‘bad, shows a closely related scene: the Prophet ﷺ asked him whether he had come to ask about righteousness, and then placed his hand on Wabisah’s chest and said, “Ask your heart, ask your soul,” and repeated it three times, then described righteousness as what the soul and the heart find at rest with, and sin as what wavers in the soul and moves in the chest, even if people give you rulings.
m: “Righteousness is good character.” The Prophet ﷺ summarised the whole subject of birr in one word: character (khuluq). Scholars say that it includes good conduct with Allah, which is to do what He loves, and with people, which is to do them good, and to avoid harming them.

“Sin is what stirs in your heart and what you dislike people finding out about.” Two marks of sin are given: unrest in the conscience, and the wish for concealment. A healthy heart reacts to wrongdoing. Scholars add a careful note: this refers to a heart that has been kept alive by faith. The one whose conscience has been blunted by sin is not a reliable measure, and must be guided by the texts of the Qur’an and Sunnah.
l: Pay attention to the unease you feel before an action, and stop to ask what it is warning you about.
Ask yourself: would I be happy for people to see this?
Work to polish your character as an act of worship.

en:
On the authority of an-Nawwas ibn Sam‘an (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Righteousness is good character, and sin is what stirs in your chest and you dislike people finding out about it.”

And on the authority of Wabisah ibn Ma‘bad (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he said: “You have come to ask about righteousness?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Consult your heart. Righteousness is what the soul feels at ease with and the heart feels at peace with; and sin is what unsettles the soul and wavers in the chest, even if people give you their ruling and keep giving it.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي نَجِيحٍ الْعِرْبَاضِ بْنِ سَارِيَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: وَعَظَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم مَوْعِظَةً وَجِلَتْ مِنْهَا الْقُلُوبُ، وَذَرَفَتْ مِنْهَا الْعُيُونُ، فَقُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ! كَأَنَّهَا مَوْعِظَةُ مُوَدِّعٍ فَأَوْصِنَا، قَالَ: أُوصِيكُمْ بِتَقْوَى اللَّهِ، وَالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ وَإِنْ تَأَمَّرَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَبْدٌ، فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ يَعِشْ مِنْكُمْ فَسَيَرَى اخْتِلَافًا كَثِيرًا، فَعَلَيْكُمْ بِسُنَّتِي وَسُنَّةِ الْخُلَفَاءِ الرَّاشِدِينَ الْمَهْدِيينَ، عَضُّوا عَلَيْهَا بِالنَّوَاجِذِ، وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَمُحْدَثَاتِ الْأُمُورِ؛ فَإِنَّ كُلَّ بِدْعَةٍ ضَلَالَةٌ.

s: Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi report this from al-‘Irbad ibn Sariyah, and at-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih. Al-‘Irbad describes the scene: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in the dawn prayer, then turned to them and delivered a sermon so moving that eyes shed tears and hearts trembled. A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, it is as if this were a farewell sermon, so advise us.”
m: His advice: “I counsel you to fear Allah, and to hear and obey, even if an Abyssinian slave is appointed over you.” Then a prediction: “Whoever of you lives will see much disagreement.” And the remedy: “Hold to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly guided caliphs after me. Bite on it with your molar teeth.” The picture of the molars suggests a firm grip: do not let go, even if pulled.

He warned against “newly invented matters”, adding that every innovation is a misguidance. Scholars interpret this as referring to additions in matters of religion. The sermon shows that unity after the Prophet is protected by the teaching and the practice of the rightly guided caliphs, Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthman and ‘Ali, and that this is a protection, not a restriction.
l: Return to the Qur’an and the Sunnah whenever people differ.
Respect legitimate leadership in what is right, and advise it privately.
Hold the Sunnah firmly, not harshly.

en: On the authority of Abu Najih al-‘Irbad ibn Sariyah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us a sermon that made the hearts tremble and the eyes flow with tears. We said: “O Messenger of Allah, it is as if this were a farewell sermon, so counsel us.” He said: “I advise you to fear Allah, and to hear and obey, even if a slave is made ruler over you. For whoever among you lives on will see much disagreement. So hold fast to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly guided caliphs after me; cling to it with your molars. And beware of newly invented matters, for every innovation is a going astray.”

ar: عَنْ مُعَاذِ بْنِ جَبَلٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قُلْت يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ! أَخْبِرْنِي بِعَمَلٍ يُدْخِلُنِي الْجَنَّةَ وَيُبَاعِدْنِي مِنْ النَّارِ، قَالَ: «لَقَدْ سَأَلْت عَنْ عَظِيمٍ، وَإِنَّهُ لَيَسِيرٌ عَلَى مَنْ يَسَّرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: تَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَتُقِيمُ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِي الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومُ رَمَضَانَ، وَتَحُجُّ الْبَيْتَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَلَا أَدُلُّك عَلَى أَبْوَابِ الْخَيْرِ؟ الصَّوْمُ جُنَّةٌ، وَالصَّدَقَةُ تُطْفِئُ الْخَطِيئَةَ كَمَا يُطْفِئُ الْمَاءُ النَّارَ، وَصَلَاةُ الرَّجُلِ فِي جَوْفِ اللَّيْلِ، ثُمَّ تَلَا: «تَتَجَافَى جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ» حَتَّى بَلَغَ» يَعْمَلُونَ «، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَلَا أُخْبِرُك بِرَأْسِ الْأَمْرِ وَعَمُودِهِ وَذُرْوَةِ سَنَامِهِ؟ قُلْت: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ. قَالَ: رَأْسُ الْأَمْرِ الْإِسْلَامُ، وَعَمُودُهُ الصَّلَاةُ، وَذُرْوَةُ سَنَامِهِ الْجِهَادُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَلَا أُخْبِرُك بِمَلَاكِ ذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ؟ فقُلْت: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ! فَأَخَذَ بِلِسَانِهِ وَقَالَ: كُفَّ عَلَيْك هَذَا. قُلْت: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ وَإِنَّا لَمُؤَاخَذُونَ بِمَا نَتَكَلَّمُ بِهِ؟ فَقَالَ: ثَكِلَتْك أُمُّك وَهَلْ يَكُبُّ النَّاسَ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ -أَوْ قَالَ عَلَى مَنَاخِرِهِمْ- إلَّا حَصَائِدُ أَلْسِنَتِهِمْ؟!».

s: At-Tirmidhi reports this from Mu‘adh ibn Jabal and grades it hasan sahih. Mu‘adh said that he was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey and had moved near him one morning. He said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me of a deed that will enter me into Paradise and keep me far from the Fire.”
The Prophet ﷺ said, “You have asked about something great, and it is easy for the one for whom Allah makes it easy.” Then he gave a conversation that is rich enough to be used as a curriculum.
m: First he gave the pillars: worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, establish prayer, give zakat, fast Ramadan and perform Hajj. Then he offered “the doors of goodness”: fasting is a shield; charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire; and a man’s prayer in the middle of the night. Then he recited the verse: “Their sides part from their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope” (32:16).

Then: “Shall I tell you the head of the matter, its pillar and its summit?” The head is Islam; the pillar is prayer; the summit of its hump is jihad (striving in the path of Allah). And finally: “Shall I tell you the key to all of that?” He took hold of his tongue and said, “Restrain this.” Mu‘adh said, “O Prophet of Allah, shall we be held to account for what we say?” He said, “May your mother lose you, Mu‘adh! Will people be thrown on their faces into the Fire for anything other than the harvest of their tongues?”
l: Take the doors of goodness as a plan: fasting, charity, night prayer.
Watch your tongue: it is called the key to all of it.
Ask the Prophet’s question to yourself: what deed will take me to Paradise?

en:
On the authority of Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me of a deed that will take me into Paradise and keep me far from the Fire.” He said: “You have asked about something great, yet it is easy for the one for whom Allah makes it easy: worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, establish the prayer, give zakat, fast Ramadan, and make the pilgrimage to the House.”

Then he said: “Shall I not guide you to the gates of goodness? Fasting is a shield; charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire; and so does a man’s prayer in the depth of the night.” Then he recited: “Their sides forsake their beds…” until he reached “…what they used to do.” Then he said: “Shall I not tell you of the head of the matter, its pillar, and its highest peak?” I said: “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is the prayer, and its highest peak is jihad.”

Then he said: “Shall I not tell you of the key to all of that?” I said: “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He took hold of his tongue and said: “Restrain this.” I said: “O Prophet of Allah, will we be held to account for what we say?” He said: “May your mother lose you, Mu‘adh! Is there anything that throws people on their faces into the Fire, or he said on their noses, except the harvest of their tongues?”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي ثَعْلَبَةَ الْخُشَنِيِّ جُرْثُومِ بن نَاشِر رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَال: «إنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى فَرَضَ فَرَائِضَ فَلَا تُضَيِّعُوهَا، وَحَدَّ حُدُودًا فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا، وَحَرَّمَ أَشْيَاءَ فَلَا تَنْتَهِكُوهَا، وَسَكَتَ عَنْ أَشْيَاءَ رَحْمَةً لَكُمْ غَيْرَ نِسْيَانٍ فَلَا تَبْحَثُوا عَنْهَا».

s: This hadith is reported by ad-Daraqutni and others from Abu Tha‘labah al-Khushani, and an-Nawawi calls it hasan. Some scholars of hadith, among them Ibn Rajab, have discussed its chain and pointed out that its meaning is supported by sound texts, so its place in the Forty is for its content, which the scholars have long relied upon.
m: It divides the religion into four categories in one sentence. Obligations (fara’id) that must not be wasted. Limits (hudud) that must not be crossed. Prohibitions (hurumat) that must not be violated. And “things about which He was silent, out of mercy for you, not forgetfulness”, which must not be asked about.

The fourth category is a gift. The basic position of things is permission, and not everything needs a ruling. The scholars used this hadith to establish that what is not addressed is left within the sphere of permission. The Qur’an says that your Lord is never forgetful (19:64). Silence is mercy, and the believer should not turn it into hardship by excessive questions and technical complications.
l: Do what is obligatory first and well, and respect the limits.
Enjoy what has not been forbidden, with gratitude.
Avoid probing for rules where Allah has allowed ease.

en: On the authority of Abu Tha‘labah al-Khushani Jurthum ibn Nashir (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: “Truly Allah the Exalted has laid down obligations, so do not neglect them; He has set limits, so do not transgress them; He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; and He has stayed silent about some things, out of mercy for you and not out of forgetfulness, so do not ask about them.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي الْعَبَّاسِ سَهْلِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ السَّاعِدِيّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ! دُلَّنِي عَلَى عَمَلٍ إذَا عَمِلْتُهُ أَحَبَّنِي اللهُ وَأَحَبَّنِي النَّاسُ؛ فَقَالَ: ازْهَدْ فِي الدُّنْيَا يُحِبَّك اللهُ، وَازْهَدْ فِيمَا عِنْدَ النَّاسِ يُحِبَّك النَّاسُ.

s: Ibn Majah and others report this from Sahl ibn Sa‘d as-Sa‘idi. A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “O Messenger of Allah, direct me to a deed which, if I do it, Allah will love me and people will love me.” The Prophet ﷺ answered with the words of the hadith. The chain is discussed by some scholars, and an-Nawawi grades it hasan.
m: “Be detached (izhad) from the world and Allah will love you; be detached from what is in people’s hands and people will love you.” Zuhd is often misunderstood as poverty or withdrawal. The early scholars explained it as emptying the heart of attachment, not the hand of possessions. Some said it is not forbidding the lawful or wasting wealth, but being more certain of what is with Allah than of what is in your own hand.

The second half is practical wisdom. People dislike the one who competes for what they have, who envies, who asks and presses. They love the one who is content and does not covet their possessions. The Prophet ﷺ taught that the upper hand is better than the lower, and that wealth is a sense of enough in the soul. Detachment has this social fruit.
l: Hold wealth in the hand, not in the heart. Be ready to give it up.
Do not look at what others have. Practise contentment and thanks.
Ask less of people, and give more.

en: On the authority of Abu al-‘Abbas Sahl ibn Sa‘d as-Sa‘idi (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “O Messenger of Allah, guide me to a deed which, if I do it, Allah will love me and people will love me.” He said: “Be detached from this world and Allah will love you; be detached from what people have and people will love you.”

ar: عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ سَعْدِ بْنِ مَالِكِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ الْخُدْرِيّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: «لَا ضَرَرَ وَلَا ضِرَارَ».

s: Ibn Majah and ad-Daraqutni report this from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, Ahmad from Ibn ‘Abbas, and Malik has it as a mursal report. Its chains are numerous and the scholars grade it hasan as a whole. Among the best-known applications is a case in Abu Dawud: Samurah ibn Jundub had a date palm in the garden of a man of the Ansar. Samurah used to come to his palm without asking permission, and it troubled the family. The Ansari complained, and the Prophet ﷺ asked Samurah to sell it, or to give it, and he refused each time. Then the Prophet ﷺ said to the Ansari, “Go and uproot his tree,” and to Samurah, “You are a harmer.”
m: “La darara wa la dirar.” Darar is to inflict harm, and dirar is to retaliate with harm, or to harm another in return, or to cause harm in a way that is a response to a disagreement. The principle is that no one may harm another, and no one may answer harm with more harm beyond what is just.

Jurists have built a great part of the law of neighbours, property, contracts and public order on this sentence. It is the source of the legal maxim that harm is to be removed (ad-darar yuzal). The same idea underlies the prohibition of fraud, the right of pre-emption, and the removal of nuisances.
l: Before you act, ask whether it will harm another person: noise, waste, blocked access, shared things.
Do not repay harm with harm. Take your right in the way the law allows.
Make peace with your neighbours and care for the commons.

en: On the authority of Abu Sa‘id Sa‘d ibn Malik ibn Sinan al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is to be no harm and no reciprocating harm.”
